methods: turning the equation into a quadratic
statement: Find the range of the function $f(x)=\\frac{x}{x^{2}+1}$ for real $x$.
solution: Set $y=\\frac{x}{x^{2}+1}$; then $yx^{2}-x+y=0$. For real $x$ the discriminant must be non-negative: $1-4y^{2}\\ge 0$, so $|y|\\le 1/2$. Both endpoints are attained: $y=1/2$ at $x=1$, $y=-1/2$ at $x=-1$. Hence the range is $[-1/2,1/2]$.
hints: Write $y=x/(x^{2}+1)$ and view it as a quadratic in $x$.
Use the discriminant condition for real $x$.
